overview.title: The Majestic Sea of Dunes
overview.p1: Erg Chebbi represents the iconic image of the Moroccan Sahara: breathtaking ridges of golden-orange sand rising up to 150 meters high, stretching across the horizon near Merzouga.
overview.p2: Visiting the dunes rewards a slower pace. Watch how the shifting sunlight transforms the colors of the sand from pale gold at noon to deep amber and fiery red at sunset.
overview.p3: Whether you explore via camel trek, 4x4 safari, or by hiking to the highest summit, Erg Chebbi offers an unforgettable wilderness experience.

tips.title: Practical Tips for Visiting Erg Chebbi

1.title: Sun & Sand Protection
1.desc: Bring sunglasses, sunscreen, and a traditional scarf (shechiah) to protect against sun and blowing sand.

2.title: Licensed Guides
2.desc: Book camel treks and 4x4 desert tours through reputable local hotels or certified camp operators.

3.title: Warm Layers
3.desc: Desert temperatures plummet after sunset — always pack a jacket or fleece for the night.

q1.question: How long do I need at Erg Chebbi?
q1.answer: Most visitors spend at least a half-day or overnight to fully experience the dunes, sunset, and sunrise.

q2.question: Is there an entrance fee for Erg Chebbi?
q2.answer: No, the sand dunes themselves are natural outdoor spaces and free to access. Guided tours, camel treks, or 4x4 rentals involve separate service fees.

q3.question: When is the best time to visit Erg Chebbi?
q3.answer: Early mornings and late afternoons offer the best lighting for photography and cooler temperatures away from midday heat.

q4.question: Can you climb the dunes?
q4.answer: Yes, climbing the high dunes (some reach up to 150 meters) is a popular activity, especially to watch the sunset.

q5.question: What should I wear when visiting the desert?
q5.answer: Light, breathable clothing for daytime, sunglasses, a scarf for wind/sun protection, and warm layers for chilly desert nights.
